title: Yangum language - Wikipedia
text: Yangum is a Torricelli dialect cluster of Papua New Guinea. Gel is nearly extinct. The principal variety is Mon, which is also known as Aiku, Malek, Menandon ~ Minendon; these names have been used for all Yangum varieties plus the closely related Ambrak.

title: Torricelli languages - Wikipedia
text: The Torricelli languages are unusual among Papuan languages in having a basic clause order of SVO (subject-verb-object); in contrast, most Papuan languages have SOV order. It was previously believed that the Torricelli word order was a result of contact with Austronesian languages, but Donohue (2005) believes it is more likely that SVO order was present in the Torricelli proto-language. title: Yangum Gel Language (YGL) - L1 & L2 Speakers, Status ... - Ethnologue
text: Yangum Gel is an endangered indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Torricelli language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.
